features.optics-sfp28: 1G fixed / 10G / 25G single-rate transceivers, AOC, DAC; 10GBASE-RJ45 supported on H/W R01G or newer

power.psus: 2x redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable AC or -48 VDC

description: 48x SFP28 + 8x QSFP28 1U ToR switch, Broadcom Trident 3 (BCM56873)

furniture.description: rack ears, flange screws, panel symbols and the underside labels - one catch-all rather than a group per kind, following the Casa chassis.

mgmt.mixed: the management cluster at the right-hand end of the faceplate - two SFP+ management uplinks (57/58), a USB-A service port, the out-of-band RJ45, the RS-232 console and a USB-C console. Five media, one job; the unit draws them as one block and so do we

name: as7326-56x

chassis.note: datasheet (Dimensions WxDxH 43.84 x 53.6 x 4.35 cm; Weight 10 kg)

entity-and-interfaces.note: read from the live unit (ArcOS S8.5.1A, netlab-leaf1) via 'show components | display json' and 'show interface brief'. Chassis serial, MAC and every per-transceiver serial are redacted from the committed dump

faceplate-structure.note: described by the owner from the unit - top two SFP rows are 2x4 ganged belly-to-belly assemblies, bottom row is 1x2 ganged in the same orientation as row 2. Visible seams measure every 2 columns (~33mm), so the drawn column geometry is unchanged by that grouping; the 2x4 spans two visual pairs. Link/activity arrows sit in the belly-to-belly gap of rows 1-2, three per column (up = row 1, down = row 2, right-hand down = row 3), and the port numbers appear ONCE per column between rows 2 and 3 as N-up / N+1-down / N+2-down - no other SFP row carries numbers

mgmt-block.note: owner - the two 10G ports are a 1x2 belly-to-belly gang with arrow LEDs between them and their label below the lower one, USB-A beneath that; the RJ45 pair is top-to-top (latches facing away from each other, not toward) with a USB-C below and the pull-out tab under that stack. The 10G pair is ports 57/58. The SFP-to-QSFP gap is ~21mm, just over one QSFP port width

port-arrangement.note: 3 rows x 16 columns confirmed on the physical unit by the owner. The datasheet panel figure is a marketing render whose column widths do not reconcile - 24 columns would need 342mm and leave no room for the mgmt block

port-count-note.note: ArcOS presents swp1-swp56 only. The faceplate labels the 10G management pair 57/58, but they are not ASIC switch ports - no swp57/58 exists

port-pitch.note: standard - SFP columns on the SFF-8433 basic 14.25, QSFP on the 19.0 measured from TE 2322551-4. The datasheet figure measures 14.45, the same ~1.4 percent scale error the S9510 HIG figure carried, so the standards are used rather than the figure

port-row-pitch.note: estimated (~14.5-15.0 to fit three rows in the 43.5mm face; the belly-to-belly reference from TE 2007562-6 is 15.0) - verify with calipers

port-speeds.note: the management jack is `1g`: the datasheet lists one RJ-45 100/1000BASE-T management port (carried in `attrs.management.mgmt-ports`).

psu-fan-reuse.note: the AC PSU FRU part numbers (F0TZZ5654019A / F0TZZ5654020A) are identical to the AS7726-32X, so common/psu-ac-650 is the same physical module

qsfp-structure.note: owner + IMG_2141 - belly-to-belly pairs labelled between the two ports of a column. The columns form two groups of two with roughly twice the separation between groups. Above the block each column carries two rows of four lane LEDs (L1-L4), the upper row belonging to the upper port, with the port number at the left of each row - the photo shows this directly

rear-layout.note: datasheet figure (PSU2 | 6 fans | PSU1, grounding point each end), geometry reused from the AS7726-32X which shares this chassis width

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 17 SFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-57/port-58). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 4 QSFP pairs (port-49/port-50 to port-55/port-56).

status-led-labels.note: drawing + photo - DIAG, LOC, PS1, PS2 and FAN are printed to the LEFT of their lamps and level with them, not beneath them: the datasheet page-2 System LEDs callout and IMG_2141 agree, and the same layout is visible on the S9510-28DC lamp stack. Right-anchored 1.3mm clear of the lamp column at x 9.2, with each baseline on its lamp centre. They were left-anchored at 12.5 under the lamps, which put DIAG into port-1

top-bottom-sides.note: extrapolated from the AS7726-32X, which shares this chassis line and its width and height, restretched to the 536mm depth. Top grooves and the centre access plate are from IMG_2129; the bottom labels from IMG_2130. Side screw and vent positions are NOT measured - reshoot on a bench to confirm
